document.name: USG
document.purpose: Define a universal, executable logic for AI-assisted generation of built structures. USG consumes a feasibility record, screens hard constraints per candidate site, and only then derives form from function, relations, topology, systems and constraints.

changelog_from_0_7: Added execution_model: the pipeline is an order of validity, not an order of work. Design may explore at any time; gates decide what may be committed. (author decision 2026-10-11)

Added phase_model: concept, schematic, design_development, technical_design, operation, mapped onto the stages, with commitment points (phase transitions, acceptance, export, irreversible acts in the world) and a commitment rule: a committed design hypothesis is blocked if any premise is negative; unknown premises pass a phase transition only under exploratory status and never pass export or an irreversible act.
Added ontology class design_hypothesis: a design idea at any stage with the question ids, claims, assumptions and affected systems it presupposes. The Design thread is the set of hypotheses.

Added awareness_model: the Awareness thread is derived from open premises of current hypotheses and unanswered questions of the current and earlier phases; ranked by dependents x severity; at most one awareness question per design turn, surfaced at a natural pause, queued and never dropped.

Added S00.drivers as the first S00 question: what triggered the project, who initiated it, who holds decision power, what each party wants. Depth follows feasibility intensity. The AI asks about drivers; it never imputes motives. Added ontology class stakeholder (parties with interests or decision power, distinct from actors who use the structure).

Added statement_model: every requirement-like statement has a statement_type (constraint, requirement, preference, assumption, open_design_variable), a basis (physical, legal, verified_site_condition, stakeholder_choice) and relaxable_by. A statement relaxable by a stakeholder is not a constraint. Added decision-layer relation pressured_by(statement, stakeholder, toward).

Added ontology class open_design_variable with owner, decide_by phase and candidate range, and the spanning rule: generators must span an open ODV, not fix it; committing a value before decide_by is a violation. Unknowns block; ODVs are protected.

Added S01.affected_systems and ontology class affected_system: baseline (evidence, confidence), change (magnitude, persistence, reversibility), beneficiaries, burden bearers, mitigation, compensation, residual. Rule: no baseline, no impact claim. Kinds include dependency and future_public_burden, the two universal questions from the settlement discussion.

Added ontology class value_perspective and evidence_model.value_rule: value is recorded as a ledger of perspectives (benefit, burden, horizon, reversibility); perspectives are shown side by side, never aggregated by the AI; weights come only from the human. S01.value now outputs the ledger.

Added schemas.strain_report: structural strain is a derived collection of open conflicts (hypothesis on a negative claim, pressure against a constraint, burden without compensation, assumption carried past its phase, ODV collapsed early). Not a status, not a score.
Added feedback loop FB9 (premise reopened): from any stage to S00 when a premise of committed work changes; escalation to the human. Inquiry stays open after commitment.

S02.site_candidates may also be answered by the human (also_answerable_by): a human-named candidate in search_area or open mode was not representable. (found while encoding the One Mile City instance)
Added stress test design_ahead_of_premise; invariants for validity order, ledger and ODV protection; open questions; next steps.

changelog: Added S01.delivery and ontology class delivery_route: how materials, equipment and labour reach the site and how the structure is built, with explicit dependencies. Added the bootstrap-cycle check to conflict_detection and as an S00/S01 gate preview: a route that depends on the intervention itself, or on an event its success condition excludes, is put back to the human as a conflict. (adversarial run: success 'built before any vehicle lands' vs delivery by that vehicle)

Added evidence_model.regulatory_absence_rule: 'no applicable regulation' is a claim that needs evidence like any other; a jurisdiction overlay may rest on a treaty, a licensing regime or an operator standard, not only on a building code. (adversarial run: 'there is no building code' accepted unchallenged)

Added professional_review_classes.reviewer_designation: where no qualified reviewer class exists for a review item, the human designates the reviewer and the designation is recorded; until then the item stays open.

Added S00.never classification: each statement is typed design_rule, use_restriction, vacuous or unevaluable on intake; vacuous and unevaluable statements go back to the human, who keeps, rewrites or drops them. Use restrictions are evaluated against lifecycle phases, not geometry. (adversarial run: a change-of-use prohibition passed unexamined)

Added inquiry_model.no_default_by_silence: the AI never fills a human-authority question with a default the human did not confirm ('unless you say otherwise' is not an answer). Added inquiry_model.site_mode_rule: a named region larger than the intervention implies search_area, to be confirmed by the human. (adversarial run: site mode set by the AI from a 4,000 km region)
Added inquiry_model.log and schemas.inquiry_log: an inquiry run records one question id per step, so granularity is checkable, not only stated. (adversarial run: three questions bundled in one step)
Added stress test bootstrap_dependency and two open questions (stage placement of constructability; reviewer designation for novel domains).

Added inquiry_model: the pipeline is executed as an inquiry, one question, one authority and one value per step; answers given early are routed to their question and never asked again; derived gate checks run as previews as soon as their inputs exist; conflicting human answers are put back to the human. (ADU run findings 10-12)

Added library_model with a library-gap path: when a domain-library value is missing, the AI may propose it as a visible assumption, the human confirms it for the project, and a generalization question decides its applicability scope (domain, jurisdiction, climate) or keeps it instance-only. Candidates are promoted only by library curation. Any open library gap keeps the project exploratory. (ADU finding 1)

Added a jurisdiction overlay layer between protocol and domain library: code obligations belong to the jurisdiction layer and enter at S09 as code rules; domain libraries hold building-type defaults only. (ADU finding 2)

Added ontology classes library_candidate, zone, lifecycle_phase and trigger_fact. Zones are contained by exactly one functional unit and are governed by fits and not_overlap; this resolves the open question on zones. (ADU findings 2, 3, 5, 6)

Added S00.lifecycle_use: the uses the structure must serve over its life, as phases with a beneficiary each (own_use, third_party_known, market, public). Replaces the separate beneficiary question proposed during the ADU run. (ADU finding 3)

Added S00.triggers: feasibility trigger facts become an explicit question. A trigger may need a fact and a professional classification; an unknown trigger applies conservatively; a library-dependent trigger with no library threshold may be asserted false by the human as a recorded assumption. (failure-run gap 1, ADU finding 5)

Added feasibility_module.intensity.own_use_rule: when the first lifecycle phase is own_use, the human's stated need is the demand evidence at any depth and existing supply means the beneficiary's own assets. Default pending author confirmation.

Added answer_authority.site_fact_rule: site facts stated by the human enter as evidence of kind owner_statement, capped at medium confidence; human authority covers site choice and confirmation, not facts a gate reads. (ADU finding 4)
Added S04.existing: existing structures, utilities, vegetation and access on the site, as context entities feeding the intervention zone, relations and rules. (ADU finding 8)
Added S06.zones: which zones share a functional unit. (ADU finding 6)
S00.never now also feeds S01, so 'never' statements filter alternatives. (ADU finding 7)
dimension_in_range gained a basis parameter (net | gross), required for area and volume. (ADU finding 9)
contains may hold zones; fits may apply to zones.
All conditional 'required' values are machine-readable ('var != value'); S01.supply and S01.demand now read 'intensity != light'. (failure-run gap 6)
evidence_model gained precedence_rule (a professional_confirmation item decides its claim; other items stay visible) and owner_statement confidence cap. (failure-run gap 2)

S02 gained status_mapping and overall_precedence (prohibited > unresolved > conditional > permitted), and scenario_rule: a prohibited site kept under a human-requested rezoning, variance or mitigation scenario continues with screen_status under_scenario, blocked from geometry unless exploratory; the scenario is a blocking review item. Scenario rule is a default pending author confirmation. (failure-run gaps 3, 5)
S01 gained decision_rules: proceeding against a confirmed_negative need claim sets project_status to exploratory. Default pending author confirmation. (failure-run gap 4)
project_status propagation: any open library-gap assumption keeps the project exploratory.
answer_authority.authorities.human text: 'human-confirmed site facts' replaced by site choice and confirmation, per site_fact_rule.
Added stress test small_private_adu, invariants for library content, scope and inquiry granularity; updated next_steps and open questions; zones question moved to resolved_questions.
Added S02.search_criteria: site search criteria come from the human, with the domain library as default; the AI proposes site candidates only within them.
Stated that only the human confirms a site candidate.
Domain libraries may add feasibility triggers or raise minimums, but never remove or lower universal triggers.
Defined site-level diversity: surviving sites are distinct by definition; graph diversity is measured only within one site.
Defined the boundary between soft rules and performance targets.
Deferred 'action' as an ontology class until a domain library shows force flows plus scenarios are insufficient.

Restored from 0.3 what 0.4 dropped: full relation definitions and properties, the 0.2 mapping, ontology fields and IFC mapping, topology_model, physics model-reference interface, geometry_model, conflict_detection, software_architecture, topology_candidate schema.
Added document_governance: each version is a patch on the previous one and must pass the checker, including a non-regression comparison.
Feasibility became a pluggable module with a required output record; its depth (light, standard, full) is set by measurable triggers with a library floor that the human may raise but not lower.
Added site_mode (given, search_area, open) and site candidates; the constraint screen runs per site; candidate hierarchy is site -> topology -> geometry.
S02 generalized from legal/land-use into a constraint screen with categories: legal_land_use, rights, environmental, heritage, infrastructure_capacity.
Removed the duplicate site question: S04.boundary is now S04.intervention_zone, derived from the S02 screen.
Added an evidence model with claims, confidence and a conflict rule: low confidence never passes a hard gate; conflicting evidence is shown, never averaged.
Added professional-review classes: blocking, deferrable, informational.
Exploratory status now propagates to the deliverable and blocks export as buildable.
Build vs non-build comparison defined as a decision record for the human, with common dimensions and no automatic winner.
Defined the five relations added in 0.4 and split the vocabulary into structure and decision layers.
Formalized intra-stage question feeds: a question may feed a later question in the same stage.

removed.reason: duplicate of S02.site_identity; replaced by derived S04.intervention_zone
merged into S02.evidence and S02.status across screen categories

document_governance.versioning: Each version is produced as a patch on the previous version, never as a full rewrite.
document_governance.non_regression: Every section, ontology class, relation and question id of the previous version must exist in the new one unless listed in changelog_removed with a reason.
document_governance.gate: A version is accepted only when check_usg.py passes, including the comparison against the previous version.
document_governance.multi_ai_review: Reviewers comment; one editor applies changes as patches. Review output is never pasted in as a new version.

core_thesis.short: Need first. Function before form. Geometry last.
core_thesis.expanded: A structure should not be designed merely because someone can imagine it. USG first asks whether a meaningful need exists, whether the proposed intervention is a sensible response, whether the use is legally and contextually possible, and whether the structure can physically and operationally work. Only then does it derive form from function, relations, topology, systems, and constraints.
core_thesis.causal_principle: Justification -> constraint screen per site -> context -> function -> requirements -> relations -> flows -> topology (with system selection) -> geometry -> system sizing -> elements -> validation.
core_thesis.execution: The pipeline is an order of validity, not an order of work: explore freely, commit only what is valid.

answer_authority.principle: Every value has exactly one authority. Values supplied by a party without authority are detectable violations. AI may propose assumptions but may not silently replace human or professional authority.

authorities.human: Purpose, priorities, preferences, confirmed project goals, acceptance, site choice and confirmation (site facts stated by the human enter as evidence, see site_fact_rule).
authorities.domain_library: Defaults, typologies, rules, benchmark ranges, and standard reasoning templates for a structure type.
authorities.ai_generated: Candidates, alternatives, synthesized evidence summaries, proposed assumptions, and design options.
authorities.professional_review: Legal applicability, zoning interpretation, code applicability, structural adequacy, life safety, and regulated professional judgments.
authorities.external_evidence: Public or private evidence such as market data, inventories, GIS, surveys, environmental studies, maps, and operating statistics.

answer_authority.assumption_rule: When a required human- or professional-authority value is unknown, AI may propose an assumption. It enters the model only as a visible assumption record and remains unresolved until confirmed or replaced.
answer_authority.evidence_rule: external_evidence supplies facts, never decisions. Whether evidence is sufficient for a gate is decided by the evidence model; interpretation of law, code or safety stays with professional_review.
answer_authority.site_rule: The AI may propose site candidates only within human- or library-sourced search criteria. A site candidate enters the screen only after human confirmation. The AI never finalizes a site.
answer_authority.site_fact_rule: A site fact stated by the human (flood zone, utilities, ground, existing structures) is recorded as evidence of kind owner_statement with at most medium confidence. It reaches high confidence only through a document or a professional confirmation. Human authority covers choosing and confirming the site, not facts that a gate reads.
answer_authority.library_gap_rule: When a required domain_library value is missing because the library is absent or incomplete, the AI may propose it as a visible assumption of kind library_gap. The human confirms it for the project, then answers the generalization question (library_model.generalization). An open library_gap assumption keeps project_status exploratory.

feasibility_module.principle: The generator core requires a feasibility record as input. Producing it is a separate, pluggable module whose depth scales with the project. USG never designs without a record whose status permits it.

levels.light: Stated need, alternatives considered, decision. No market evidence required.
levels.standard: Light plus existing-supply and demand evidence at medium confidence.
levels.full: Standard plus quantified gap, value case, and an alternatives decision record with all comparison dimensions.

triggers.condition: public assembly, regulated or high-risk occupancy
size or cost above library threshold

intensity.authority: Derived from universal triggers plus library triggers. The resulting minimum is the floor; the human may raise the level but never lower it below that floor.
intensity.library_extension: A domain library may add triggers or raise the minimum of an existing trigger. It may never remove a universal trigger or lower a universal minimum.
intensity.unknown_rule: An unknown trigger fact applies conservatively: the floor is never lowered by an unknown. A trigger whose threshold only a library can set (size or cost above library threshold) may be asserted false by the human when no library threshold exists; the assertion is a recorded assumption in the strategic feasibility record.
intensity.trigger_fact_rule: A trigger may combine a fact (human or external_evidence) with a classification (professional_review), e.g. 'care visits occur' and 'this is a regulated occupancy'. Until classified, the trigger is unknown and the unknown_rule applies.

own_use_rule.rule: When the first lifecycle phase has beneficiary own_use, the human's stated need (S01.need) is the demand evidence at any depth, and existing supply means the beneficiary's own assets (stated as owner_statement evidence). Market evidence is not required.

pipeline.name: purpose
pipeline.purpose: Define what the proposed structure would do and what success means.

questions.q: What triggered this project, who initiated it, who holds decision power, and what does each party want?
What is this structure for?
What would success look like?
What must it never do or be?

meaning.design_rule: evaluable on candidates; becomes a hard rule at S09.never
meaning.use_restriction: evaluable on lifecycle phases and permitted uses, not on geometry
meaning.vacuous: no candidate or phase could violate it; adds no constraint
meaning.unevaluable: cannot be expressed with the relation vocabulary or a lifecycle check

classification.rule: Each statement is classified on intake (derived, shown to the human). Vacuous and unevaluable statements go back to the human, who keeps, rewrites or drops them; kept ones are recorded with kept_by_human. The protocol classifies statements; it never judges them as unreasonable.

questions.q: Which domain library applies, and which version?
Is the site given, to be chosen within a search area, or fully open?
Which uses must the structure serve over its life, in which phases, and for whom?
Which feasibility trigger conditions apply to this project, as facts (public funding or ownership, regulated occupancy, size or cost, off-site impact, library triggers)?

pipeline.gate: Purpose, success criteria, site mode, lifecycle use and trigger facts stated; library pinned or declared as a draft.

pipeline.name: strategic_feasibility
pipeline.purpose: Obtain or produce the feasibility record at the required depth. Executed by the feasibility module.

questions.q: Which feasibility depth applies (light, standard, full)?
What unmet need or problem does the proposed structure address?
How do materials, equipment and labour reach the site, and how is the structure built? Does any route depend on the structure itself, or on an event the success criteria exclude?
Which systems outside the intervention does it change, what is their baseline, and who benefits or bears the burden?
What existing facilities, assets, or systems already provide the same or similar function?
What evidence supports current or future demand?
What capacity, service, location, quality, resilience, access, or performance gap remains unmet?
Could the need be met better by doing nothing, reuse, adaptation, expansion, relocation, or operational change?
What economic, social, strategic, operational, environmental, or resilience value would this intervention create?
Is there sufficient justification to proceed to feasibility and design?

pipeline.gate: Proceed if the human accepts the justification at the required depth. If rejected, stop. If explicitly exploratory, continue with project_status = exploratory.

decision_rules.proceed_against_negative_need: If the human decides proceed while a need claim at S01 is confirmed_negative, project_status becomes exploratory and the gate is recorded as passed under exploratory status.

pipeline.name: constraint_screen
pipeline.purpose: Screen every candidate site for show-stopping constraints before context, function or geometry. Runs once per site candidate.

questions.q: Within which limits may site candidates be searched (area, distance, size, access, cost, exclusions)?
Which site candidates satisfy the search criteria? (given: the one site; search_area or open: AI proposes candidates within S02.search_criteria only) The human may also name candidates.
What parcel, water area, corridor, easement or boundary defines each candidate?
What evidence exists for each screen category at each candidate?
For each candidate and category: permitted, conditional, unresolved or prohibited?
Which approvals, variances, permits, rights or conditions are required?

gate.any_conditional: candidate continues; every condition becomes an explicit constraint
gate.any_unresolved: candidate blocked from geometry unless project_status = exploratory
gate.any_prohibited: candidate dropped, unless the human requests a rezoning, variance or mitigation scenario
gate.no_candidate_survives: stop; return to S00 via FB7 with the screen records

status_mapping.note: Category status follows evidence_model.gate_mapping of its claims: any confirmed_negative claim -> fail; any conflicting or insufficient claim, or no claim -> unresolved; otherwise pass.

scenario_rule.rule: A prohibited candidate kept under a human-requested rezoning, variance or mitigation scenario continues with screen_status under_scenario. It is blocked from geometry unless project_status is exploratory, and the scenario is a blocking professional-review item.

pipeline.name: actors
pipeline.purpose: Identify who or what uses, moves through, loads, services, or interacts with the structure.

questions.q: Who or what uses, occupies, loads, moves through, or services the structure?

pipeline.gate: At least one actor; every actor type exists in the domain library.

pipeline.name: context
pipeline.purpose: Describe where the structure exists and the external conditions that constrain it.

questions.q: What already exists on the site: structures, utilities and connections, vegetation to keep or remove, access routes?
questions.if_unknown: explicit unknown; blocks the stages that need it

questions.q: Within each surviving site, where may intervention occur (setbacks, easements, exclusion zones)?
What is the orientation reference: north, flow direction, alignment, channel, street, or other datum?
Where can actors, goods, services, utilities, vessels, vehicles, or pedestrians enter or connect?
Which environmental conditions apply: terrain, soil, water, bathymetry, wind, climate, hazards, ecology?
Budget, schedule, material, construction, operational, access, or phasing constraints?

pipeline.gate: Required context known or explicitly assumed.

pipeline.name: scenarios
pipeline.purpose: Define operating states, design events, and phases the structure must function in or survive.

questions.q: Which normal operating states matter?
Which design events must it survive?
Are construction, staged-use, seasonal, or temporary phases relevant?

pipeline.gate: Every capacity and physics rule references at least one scenario.

pipeline.name: functions
pipeline.purpose: Define what activities and processes the structure must host.

questions.q: Which functions must it host, and how many of each?
Do units of the same type have distinct roles?
Which functional units or zones are implied but not explicitly requested?
Which zones share a functional unit, and which unit contains each zone?

pipeline.gate: Every referenced unit, zone, role, group, and implicit function is declared; every zone is contained by exactly one unit.

pipeline.name: capacity
pipeline.purpose: Quantify demand, size, throughput, occupancy, loading, and other required capacities.

questions.q: What demand must each unit and flow carry in each scenario?
What overall size, capacity, span, area, volume, throughput, or footprint budget applies?

pipeline.gate: Minimum demand is feasible within any stated global size or capacity budget.

pipeline.name: relations
pipeline.purpose: Define how units, actors, systems, flows, and context entities connect, separate, support, and interact.

questions.q: Which relations does the domain library prescribe?
Which flows exist, with source, sink, medium, direction, and capacity?
Does the client change any default relation?

pipeline.gate: All relation endpoints declared; no hard contradictions.

pipeline.name: physics_and_regulation
pipeline.purpose: Compile physical actions, governing models, codes, safety rules, and site-specific approval conditions.

questions.q: Which physical actions act on the structure in each scenario?
Which physics models evaluate those actions, and at which stage can each run?
Which codes and standards govern, in which jurisdiction and edition?
Translate land-use approvals and conditions from S02 into hard or soft project rules.
Translate design_rule statements from S00 into evaluable hard rules and use_restriction statements into lifecycle checks; carry kept vacuous or unevaluable statements to provenance.

pipeline.gate: Every rule is sourced, scenario-aware where applicable, and has a declared evaluable stage.

pipeline.name: performance
pipeline.purpose: Define what qualities should be optimized among otherwise valid candidates.

questions.q: Which performance targets matter, and how is each measured?
How should the client's priorities reweight domain-library defaults?
How should the strategic-feasibility value case influence candidate scoring?

pipeline.gate: Scoring weights sum to 1.0; every score group has a metric or soft rule.

pipeline.name: semantic_model
pipeline.purpose: Assemble the complete pre-topology model and detect conflicts before form generation.

questions.q: Assemble the semantic model and run conflict detection.

pipeline.gate: No unresolved hard conflicts; no unknown required for topology.

pipeline.name: topology_generation
pipeline.purpose: Generate structurally distinct organizational candidates without continuous coordinates.

questions.q: Which system options fit the semantic model?
Which graph arrangements satisfy topology-stage hard rules?

pipeline.gate: At least the library minimum number of diverse valid candidates.

pipeline.name: topology_validation
pipeline.purpose: Validate every candidate against topology-stage hard rules.

questions.q: Does each topology candidate pass every hard rule evaluable at topology stage?

pipeline.gate: At least one valid topology.

pipeline.name: geometry_generation
pipeline.purpose: Create dimensioned geometric realizations from valid topologies.

questions.q: Generate envelope, functional-unit geometry, circulation, system paths, boundaries, openings, and spatial clearances.
Which geometric reference convention applies?

pipeline.gate: Each realization passes all geometry-stage hard rules.

pipeline.name: system_sizing
pipeline.purpose: Size selected systems against all scenarios.

questions.q: Size structure, enclosure, services, navigation, circulation, drainage, or other selected systems.

pipeline.gate: System capacities and physical flows close or are explicitly flagged.

pipeline.name: elements
pipeline.purpose: Derive physical elements from geometry and systems.

questions.q: Derive physical elements, each with a host, owner, or system.

pipeline.gate: No orphan element.

pipeline.name: independent_validation
pipeline.purpose: Independently test all hard constraints and scenario-dependent rules.

questions.q: Check every hard rule at its declared evaluable stage across all scenarios.
List every unresolved or professional-review item.

pipeline.gate: Any failed hard rule rejects the candidate.

pipeline.name: scoring
pipeline.purpose: Rank surviving candidates against soft performance, strategic value, and human priorities.

questions.q: Score surviving candidates using soft rules, performance metrics, and reweighted priorities.

pipeline.gate: Scores trace to metrics/rules; multiple diverse valid candidates remain where possible.

pipeline.name: human_acceptance
pipeline.purpose: Require explicit human choice before deliverable export.

questions.q: Which candidate is accepted, and are assumptions confirmed?

pipeline.gate: Explicit acceptance.

pipeline.name: export
pipeline.purpose: Produce the requested deliverable with full provenance.

questions.q: Which formats and level of detail are required?
Attach the provenance, feasibility, assumptions, loops, and review record.

pipeline.gate: Deliverable includes provenance and feasibility status.

feasibility_model.principle: A project may proceed to geometry only if strategic and legal feasibility are passed or explicitly carried as exploratory. A failed project is not rescued by geometry.

alternatives_to_build.principle: New construction is one possible intervention, not the default answer.

comparison.form: decision record for the human; no automatic winner
comparison.rule: Every alternative is described on the same dimensions at the same depth; missing values are marked unknown, not omitted.
comparison.note: Lifecycle cost and carbon appear here at coarse resolution and again as performance targets at design resolution.

actor.definition: An entity that uses, occupies, moves through, loads, services, or otherwise interacts with the structure.
actor.ifc: IfcActor (people/organizations only); other actors carried as properties or load definitions

context_entity.definition: An external condition or object that constrains or interacts with the structure.

scenario.definition: A state the structure must perform in or survive: an operating condition, a load case, a design event, or a phase.
scenario.ifc: IfcStructuralLoadCase / IfcStructuralLoadGroup for load cases; otherwise none

functional_unit.definition: A spatial or operational region defined by purpose, capacity, and required relations.

flow.definition: Movement of people, matter, energy, information, or force through or across the structure. Always a first-class entity; relations reference flows, never replace them.
flow.note: A force flow is a load path. supported_by is derived from force flows.
flow.ifc: IfcDistributionSystem for services; IfcStructuralAnalysisModel for force; circulation has no direct class

quantity.definition: A measured demand, capacity or size attached to a unit, flow, actor or the whole structure, optionally per scenario.

system.definition: A coordinated mechanism by which the structure works. Selected at topology, sized after geometry.

element.definition: A physical component derived from geometry and systems. Always has a host or owning system.

performance_target.definition: A measurable quality the design should achieve, linked to a metric and a score group.

rule.definition: An evaluable statement over entities using one relation from the vocabulary.

assumption.definition: A value proposed in place of an unknown human- or professional-authority value.

unknown.definition: A required value with no answer and no accepted assumption.

source.definition: Where a value or rule came from.

evidence.definition: An observation, dataset, inventory, study, statistic, survey, map or record used to support or contradict a claim.

kind_reserved.owner_statement: A fact stated by the owner or client; confidence at most medium.
kind_reserved.professional_confirmation: A confirmation by a qualified professional; decides its claim (evidence_model.precedence_rule).

claim.definition: A proposition a gate needs to decide, e.g. 'residential use is permitted at site A' or 'unmet demand exceeds 200 units'.

intervention_alternative.definition: A possible response to the identified need, including non-build options.

site_candidate.definition: A possible location for the structure, with its own constraint screen record.

zone.definition: A region inside a functional unit defined by an activity and its clearances (e.g. kitchen, sleeping and dining zones of a studio). Contained by exactly one functional unit.

lifecycle_phase.definition: A period of use with its own beneficiary; the first phase justifies the intervention, later phases are retained options.

trigger_fact.definition: The fact and, where needed, the professional classification that decide one feasibility trigger.

library_candidate.definition: A value proposed during a library-gap inquiry that the human declared valid beyond one project. Becomes library content only through library curation.

delivery_route.definition: A way materials, equipment or labour reach the site, with what it depends on. 'self' marks a dependency on the intervention itself; 'success_condition' marks a dependency on an event the success criteria exclude.

design_hypothesis.definition: A design idea at any level of definition (a section, a system concept, a layout), recorded with what it presupposes.
design_hypothesis.presupposes_note: question ids, claim ids, assumption ids, affected_system ids or ODV ids

stakeholder.definition: A party with interests in or decision power over the project (initiator, financier, operator, authority, community). Distinct from actors, who use or load the structure.

open_design_variable.definition: A question intentionally left open to preserve exploration. Unlike an unknown it does not block; it is protected until its decide_by phase.

affected_system.definition: A system outside the intervention that it changes: ecology, water, ground, ice, atmosphere, climate, community, infrastructure, economy, labour, a dependency it creates, or a burden it shifts to the future.
affected_system.rule: No baseline, no impact claim: with no baseline evidence, change.magnitude is 'unresolved', never zero or a value.

value_perspective.definition: One row of the value ledger: what the intervention means for one stakeholder, actor or affected system.

property_meaning.inverse: Name of the derived inverse relation; never stored, always computed.
property_meaning.earliest_stage: First stage at which the relation can be evaluated.

layers.structure: Relations among entities of the structure and its context; evaluated on candidates.
layers.decision: Relations among claims, evidence, alternatives and permissions; evaluated in feasibility and screening.

adjacent.definition: a and b share a boundary.
adjacent.subject: unit

separated_from.definition: a and b do not share a boundary, optionally with a minimum distance or separation type.

params.type: fire | acoustic | privacy | hygiene | structural | null

separated_from.subject: unit | flow | element

within_distance.definition: distance between a and b is at most d.
within_distance.subject: any spatial entity

aligned_with.definition: a is aligned with b along an axis or reference.
aligned_with.subject: unit | element | system

connected_to.definition: a direct connection exists between a and b, optionally through a named element.
connected_to.subject: unit

reachable.definition: a path exists from a to b for the given actor, optionally avoiding listed entities.
reachable.subject: unit | context_entity

serves.definition: a provides function or service to b.
serves.subject: system | unit

part_of.definition: a is a component or member of b.
part_of.subject: unit | element | system

hosted_by.definition: element a is physically carried in element b (opening in wall).
hosted_by.subject: element

traverses.definition: flow a passes through entity b.
traverses.subject: flow

supported_by.definition: a force flow from a reaches b. Derived from force flows; may also be stated as a requirement.
supported_by.subject: element | system | unit

exposed_to.definition: a is subject to action or condition b in a scenario, optionally mitigated.
exposed_to.subject: unit | element | system

resists.definition: a withstands action b in scenario s within a utilization limit.
resists.subject: element | system

fits.definition: required zones or equipment fit inside a without mutual overlap.
fits.subject: unit | zone

not_overlap.definition: a and b do not intersect, optionally keeping a clearance.
not_overlap.subject: zone | element | unit

not_cross.definition: path or flow a does not pass through zone b.
not_cross.subject: flow | zone

dimension_in_range.definition: a measured dimension of a lies within [min, max].

params.measure: width | length | height | area | volume | span | depth | clearance_height
params.basis: net | gross | null (required when measure is area or volume)

dimension_in_range.subject: unit | element | system

has_exterior_boundary.definition: a has at least the given length or count of boundary facing the exterior or a named context entity.
has_exterior_boundary.subject: unit

has_opening.definition: a has at least n openings of a type on a boundary of a type.
has_opening.subject: unit

evidenced_by.definition: claim or value a is supported or contradicted by evidence b.
evidenced_by.subject: claim | quantity | rule

competes_with.definition: existing asset or provider a meets some of the same need as proposed structure b.
competes_with.subject: context_entity | intervention_alternative

substitutes_for.definition: alternative a could meet the need instead of alternative b.
substitutes_for.subject: intervention_alternative

permitted_by.definition: use, structure or site a is allowed by regulation, approval or right b.
permitted_by.subject: site_candidate | functional_unit | intervention_alternative

conditioned_by.definition: permission a holds only if condition b is met; b becomes a rule.
conditioned_by.subject: claim | site_candidate

pressured_by.definition: statement a is being pushed by stakeholder b toward a stronger statement type (usually preference -> requirement).
pressured_by.subject: statement | rule

fields.subject: entity, type, role, group, system, element, flow, evidence item, or intervention
fields.object: entity, type, role, group, system, element, flow, evidence item, intervention, or null
fields.source_class: physics | code | accessibility | purpose | context | design_guidance | preference | market | strategic | environmental | legal
fields.source_ref: citation, library path, question id, evidence id, or model reference
fields.clause: required for code/standard sources when available
fields.evaluable_stage: strategic | legal | semantic | topology | geometry | system | final
fields.site_scope: all sites or list of site candidate ids

logic.hard_rule: Violation in any listed scenario rejects the candidate at the rule's evaluable_stage.
logic.soft_rule: Violation lowers the score of its score_group.
logic.placeholder_rule: Accepted for exploration, always listed in provenance.
logic.not_yet_evaluable: A hard rule that cannot run at the current stage is carried forward; it never passes by default.

soft_rule_vs_performance_target.soft_rule: A predicate (satisfied or not) evaluated per instance; its score group is scored by the weighted share of satisfied instances.
soft_rule_vs_performance_target.performance_target: A continuous metric with a direction (maximize, minimize, target); scored by normalized distance to the best or target value.
soft_rule_vs_performance_target.conversion: A performance target with a threshold becomes a rule: hard if the threshold must be met, soft if it is preferred (satisficing).
soft_rule_vs_performance_target.test: If the natural answer is yes/no, it is a rule. If the natural answer is a number to improve, it is a performance target.

controlled_feedback_loops.principle: The pipeline is causal, but only declared feedback loops are allowed.

loops.reason: Physics or regulation requires different relation logic.
Selected systems cannot be sized within limits.
Strategic feasibility reveals that the proposed purpose needs reframing.
No site candidate survives the constraint screen.
No valid topology exists on any surviving site; another site candidate may be needed.
A premise of committed work has changed or been reopened (new evidence, changed driver, changed affected-system baseline).

controlled_feedback_loops.restriction: No loop silently changes purpose, site, legal status, human priorities, or confirmed assumptions.

escalation.trigger: No loop can resolve a hard conflict without changing a human-authority value, or max_iterations is reached.
escalation.action: Stop and present the conflict report with resolution options to the human. The AI never applies the change itself.

early_stop_logic.strategic_fail: stop unless human explicitly requests exploratory study
early_stop_logic.physical_infeasible: stop or return to human with alternatives
early_stop_logic.no_valid_topology: return conflict report; do not force geometry
early_stop_logic.screen_prohibited_all_sites: stop unless the human requests a rezoning, variance or mitigation scenario
early_stop_logic.screen_unresolved: block geometry for that site unless exploratory

independence.definition: The validator receives only the rule set, scenarios, physics model references, evidence and claims, feasibility and screen records, and the candidate model. It never receives generator reasoning, prompts or intermediate states.
independence.consequence: A validator may be a different program or a different AI, and the result must be identical for the same inputs.

legal: every screen category has evidence or is marked insufficient
final: project_status consistent with open blocking items

strategic_feasibility_record.alternatives_decision_record: per alternative: values on every comparison dimension

provenance.answers: every question id with value, authority and source
provenance.evidence: every evidence item used in strategic/legal feasibility
provenance.project_status: real | exploratory, with every gate passed under exploratory status
provenance.review_items: every professional-review item with its class and status

topology_candidate.graphs: map<graph type, {nodes: list<entity id>, edges: list<{a, b, relation, params}>}>

inquiry_log.steps: list<{step, asked: question_id, routed: list<question_id>, authority, answer_ref}>

strain_report.note: Derived, never stored; counted per category, never collapsed into one number.

must_not_define: project-specific quantities except as labeled defaults
jurisdiction-specific code obligations (they belong in a jurisdiction overlay)
domain_library_requirements.site_search_criteria_note: Library search criteria are defaults for S02.search_criteria; the human may replace them.

domain_stress_tests.small_private: Does a private shed or single house pass through light feasibility and a one-site screen without heavy process?
domain_stress_tests.residential: Can USG derive a usable dwelling layout before walls are created?
domain_stress_tests.bridge: Can USG select the structural system with topology and derive spans, supports and clearances before geometry?
domain_stress_tests.harbor: Can USG compare site candidates, screen environmental constraints, and derive basins, berths and protection from vessel and water requirements?
domain_stress_tests.unjustified_or_prohibited: Does USG stop before geometry when need fails or every site is prohibited?
domain_stress_tests.small_private_adu: Does a backyard ADU with no library reach the design stages as exploratory through library-gap inquiry, without market evidence?
domain_stress_tests.bootstrap_dependency: Does USG surface, before S02, a delivery route that depends on the structure itself or on an event its success criteria exclude?
domain_stress_tests.design_ahead_of_premise: When design runs ahead of a show-stopping premise, does USG let exploration continue, rank the premise first, report strain, and block commitment?

invariants: Need is tested before design, at a depth set by measurable triggers.
New construction is not the default answer.
Purpose and justification are different questions.
Show-stopping constraints are screened per site before geometry.
The site may be given, searched or open; it is never silently assumed.
The AI never finalizes a site; search criteria come from the human or the domain library.
Function first, geometry second.
Every value has exactly one authority.
No downstream stage silently invents upstream information.
Unknowns remain unknown or become explicit assumptions.
Low-confidence or conflicting evidence never passes a hard gate.
Every capacity and physics rule is scenario-aware.
Physical elements are derived, not drawn first.
Hard rules are gates; not-yet-evaluable hard rules never pass by default.
Soft rules are scored.
Systems are selected with topology and sized after geometry.
Generation and validation are separate.
Only declared feedback loops are allowed.
Exploratory results can never be exported as buildable.
Every rule, answer, condition and evidence item is source-traceable.
Multiple diverse candidates survive at each level until scoring.
Domain knowledge lives in libraries, not in the universal protocol.
Each version is a patch on the previous one and passes the non-regression check.
Library content is never created silently: every library value comes from a released library or a visible library-gap assumption.
Every library candidate carries an applicability scope; code obligations belong to the jurisdiction layer, not to a domain library.
One question, one authority, one value per inquiry step.
No human-authority value is set by silence.
Absence of regulation is evidenced, never assumed.
Constructability is tested before design: every structure needs at least one delivery route that does not depend on itself.
The pipeline is an order of validity: exploration is free, commitment is gated.
Value perspectives are shown side by side, never aggregated by the AI.
Open design variables are protected, not defaulted.
Drivers are asked, never imputed.

open_questions_for_review: Are the universal feasibility triggers complete, or is a trigger missing that every library would have to add?
Are the five screen categories sufficient for all structure types?
Is graph edit distance a sufficient diversity measure within a site, or is a functional measure needed?
own_use_rule: is the human's stated need sufficient demand evidence at every depth, or only at light depth? (default: every depth)
S01.decision_rules: should proceeding against a confirmed_negative need force exploratory status, or be allowed as a recorded override? (default: exploratory)
S02.scenario_rule: is under_scenario the right status for a prohibited site kept under a human-requested scenario? (default: yes, blocked from geometry unless exploratory)
Design events: are event types universal for a domain and only their magnitudes jurisdictional?
Should constructability (S01.delivery) stay in S01, or become part of a separate physical-feasibility stage?
Reviewer designation: may the human designate any reviewer, or must the jurisdiction overlay or library set minimum qualifications?
Awareness ranking: is dependents x severity sufficient, or does irreversibility need its own factor?
Should the operation phase get its own stages (verification, adaptation), or stay a feedback channel?
Driver depth: are trigger and initiator enough at light depth?

topology_model.definition: A topology candidate is a set of typed graphs plus a system selection, with no continuous coordinates. It always belongs to exactly one site candidate.

graph_types.adjacency: units as nodes, shared boundaries as edges with connection type
graph_types.circulation: units and access points as nodes, reachable paths as edges, per actor
graph_types.flow_network: per medium: sources, sinks and traversed entities
graph_types.support: elements or systems as nodes, force flow as edges
graph_types.sequence: ordered chain of units along an axis (spans, berths, process steps)

topology_model.library_declares: Which graph types are required for its structure type. Residential: containment, adjacency, circulation, flow_network. Bridge: sequence, support, flow_network. Harbor: containment, circulation, flow_network, sequence.

candidate_strategy.diversity_measure: normalized graph edit distance per graph type, plus a different system selection counts as distinct
candidate_strategy.diversity_floor: library default; candidates closer than the floor are merged
candidate_strategy.site_level_diversity: Different surviving site candidates are distinct by definition. Graph diversity is measured only between topology candidates on the same site.
candidate_strategy.odv_spanning: Topology candidates must differ along every open design variable until its decide_by phase.

topology_model.candidate_hierarchy: site_candidate -> topology_candidate -> geometric_candidate; diversity is measured within each level.

dual_role.as_stage: S09 identifies actions per scenario and the models that evaluate them.
dual_role.as_rules: Physics produces hard rules (resists, supported_by) and performance metrics.

model_reference.principle: Physics models are referenced by interface, not by solver, so any solver satisfying the interface can be used.

fields.inputs: list of semantic model fields consumed

principles: Spaces or functional zones before walls.
Boundaries derived from stable functional boundaries.
Access openings derived from circulation graph.
Environmental openings placed after boundaries are stable.
Every element has a host or owning system.
Every geometric entity traces back to a semantic entity id.

checks: contradictory hard relations (e.g. adjacent and separated_from on the same pair)
impossible separation (more separations than available boundary)
rules referencing undeclared entities or scenarios
bootstrap cycle: a delivery route depends on the intervention itself or on an event its success criteria exclude
conflict_detection.bootstrap_rule: If every delivery route depends on 'self' or 'success_condition', the conflict is put back to the human (inquiry_model.conflicts) before S02; the AI never resolves it by changing the success criteria or inventing a route. If at least one independent route exists, the dependent routes are recorded and the run continues. The check runs as a gate preview as soon as S00.success and S01.delivery are answered.

software_architecture.protocol: This document: stages, authorities, ontology, relations, rule model, schemas.
software_architecture.domain_library: Structure-type knowledge: residential, harbor, bridge, warehouse, hospital, offshore, industrial.
software_architecture.program_instance: One project: answers, context, functions, quantities, overrides, assumptions.
software_architecture.scorer: Ranks valid candidates by soft rules, metrics and priorities.
software_architecture.exporter: Maps semantic and geometry models to JSON, IFC, OBJ, STL, Rhino, Revit.
software_architecture.feasibility_module: Produces the strategic feasibility record at the required depth; replaceable.
software_architecture.evidence_store: Holds evidence and claims with confidence and sources.
software_architecture.jurisdiction_overlay: Code obligations and land-use rules per jurisdiction; shared across domain libraries.
software_architecture.inquiry_engine: Executes inquiry_model: next question, routing, gate previews, library-gap inquiries.

evidence_model.principle: Evidence supports or contradicts claims. Gates read claim status, never raw evidence.

claim_status_rule.confirmed_positive: at least one high-confidence supporting item and no high-confidence contradicting item
claim_status_rule.confirmed_negative: at least one high-confidence contradicting item and no high-confidence supporting item
claim_status_rule.insufficient: only medium or low confidence evidence, or none

gate_mapping.confirmed_positive: pass (still subject to professional confirmation if the question requires it)
gate_mapping.conflicting: unresolved; all sides shown in the conflict report

rules: Low-confidence evidence never passes a hard gate.
Conflicting evidence is presented side by side, never averaged or silently ranked.
Evidence with a valid_until date in the past is treated as low confidence.
A professional confirmation may resolve a conflicting or insufficient claim; it is recorded as its own evidence item.
Evidence of kind owner_statement never exceeds medium confidence.
evidence_model.precedence_rule: An evidence item of kind professional_confirmation decides the status of the claim it supports or contradicts (supports -> confirmed_positive, contradicts -> confirmed_negative). All other items remain listed and visible. Two professional confirmations in opposite directions leave the claim conflicting.
evidence_model.regulatory_absence_rule: A statement that no regulation, code or standard applies is a claim (gate S02 or S09). It needs evidence like any other claim and is never assumed. A jurisdiction overlay may rest on a treaty, a licensing regime, an operator standard or a contractual specification, not only on a building code.
evidence_model.value_rule: Value is a ledger of perspectives. Perspectives are shown side by side and never aggregated, ranked or netted by the AI. Weights come only from the human (S10.priorities). The ledger reveals; it does not judge.

blocking.meaning: Nothing downstream may treat the item as resolved until a qualified person confirms. Exploratory runs may proceed but cannot export as buildable.

deferrable.meaning: May remain open during design; must be closed before export as buildable.

reviewer_designation.meaning: Where no recognised qualified reviewer class exists for a review item (novel structure type, new jurisdiction), the human designates the reviewer and the designation is recorded with the item. Until a reviewer is designated, the item stays open.

project_status.set_by: human, at S01.decision or when continuing past a failed or unresolved gate
propagation: Every gate passed under exploratory status is recorded with the reason it would otherwise have stopped.
Exploratory deliverables are marked on every sheet, model and export.
An exploratory deliverable can never be exported as buildable or for construction.
Changing exploratory to real requires every blocking item to be resolved.
Any open library_gap assumption keeps project_status exploratory.

question_record_schema.required: true | false | machine-readable condition 'var != value' or 'var == value'
question_record_schema.feeds: stage ids, or question ids in the same stage that come later in the list

ontology_decisions.topic: action as a separate ontology class
ontology_decisions.current_model: actions are represented by scenarios, force flows and physics model references
ontology_decisions.revisit_when: a domain library cannot express a required load or action without it; the bridge library is the first test

inquiry_model.principle: The pipeline is executed as an inquiry: the engine returns the next applicable, unanswered question in causal order and evaluates each gate as soon as its inputs are complete.
inquiry_model.granularity: One question, one authority, one value per step. A step never bundles questions with different authorities or different decisions.

routing.external_evidence: collect evidence (search, documents supplied by the human); record kind, source, date and confidence
routing.professional_review: record a review item stating what must be confirmed and by whom
routing.ai_generated: propose; the human confirms where the question requires confirmation
routing.domain_library: use the pinned library value; if missing, open a library-gap inquiry (library_model.library_gap)

inquiry_model.answer_routing: An answer given before its question is reached is recorded against its question id with the stage it was received in, and that question is not asked again. It is evaluated when its stage's gate runs.
inquiry_model.gate_preview: A derived check may run as soon as its inputs exist, at the human's request or by the engine. Its result is informational until the owning stage is reached.
inquiry_model.conflicts: Contradictory answers under human authority are put back to the human as a conflict question. The AI never chooses between them.
inquiry_model.ambiguity: An answer that can be read two ways is confirmed with the human before it is recorded.
inquiry_model.no_default_by_silence: The AI never fills a human-authority question with a value the human did not confirm. 'Unless you say otherwise' is not an answer; the question stays open or becomes a visible assumption awaiting confirmation.
inquiry_model.site_mode_rule: A named region larger than the intervention (a valley, district, coastline, corridor) implies site_mode search_area, to be confirmed by the human. A site is given only when its boundary is identified.
inquiry_model.log: Every inquiry run records an inquiry_log. Each step asks exactly one question id; a step may record several question ids only when one human answer is routed to several questions (answer_routing).

layer_meaning.protocol: universal logic; no domain or jurisdiction knowledge
layer_meaning.jurisdiction_overlay: code obligations, editions, design magnitudes and land-use rules for a jurisdiction; read at S02 and S09; reusable across domain libraries; may rest on a treaty, licensing regime, operator standard or contract where no building code exists
layer_meaning.domain_library: building-type defaults: actor types, unit and zone types, default relations, scenarios, benchmarks
layer_meaning.program_instance: one project's answers, assumptions and evidence

steps: AI proposes a value for the missing library question as an assumption of kind library_gap
human confirms or changes it for this project
generalization question: valid for this project only, or valid within a scope (domain, jurisdiction, climate)
scoped values become library_candidate records; project-only values stay in the instance
library_gap.status_effect: any open library_gap assumption keeps project_status exploratory

generalization.question: Is this value valid only for this project, or for every structure of this type within a scope?

library_model.code_obligations: A requirement that comes from a code is never a library default. It enters at S09.codes as a rule with source_class code, edition and clause, scoped to its jurisdiction.

curation.authority: library editor (human), with professional_review for code-like or safety content
curation.rule: Candidates are promoted only in a library release; never automatically. A candidate keeps its basis (single_instance until confirmed by further instances or a professional).
curation.release: A library release is versioned and pinned by instances at S00.library.

resolved_questions.question: Should zones be a separate class or functional units with a zone role?
resolved_questions.answer: Separate class, contained by exactly one functional unit (ontology.zone).
resolved_questions.evidence: ADU run: studio with kitchen, sleeping and dining zones in one unit

execution_model.principle: The stage order defines what a value or design decision depends on, not when it may be thought of. Design hypotheses may be created at any time; gates decide what may be committed.

threads.design: the set of design_hypothesis records: what is being explored or shaped
threads.inquiry: inquiry_model: the next question needed to continue
threads.awareness: awareness_model: derived from open premises and unvisited dimensions

execution_model.single_state: The three threads are views over one project state, not separate engines.

phase_model.operation_note: Operation follows export: verification, adaptation and lifecycle feedback into library curation and FB9.
phase_model.irreversible_act: An act in the world that is costly to undo (land purchase, permit filing, procurement, construction start), declared by the human.

commitment_rule.negative: A committed hypothesis with any premise confirmed_negative, failed or prohibited is blocked, unless the premise is held under a human-requested scenario.
commitment_rule.unresolved: A premise that is unknown, insufficient or conflicting passes a phase transition only under exploratory status, recorded with the reason; it never passes acceptance, export or an irreversible act.
commitment_rule.odv: Committing a value for an open design variable before its decide_by phase is a violation.

statement_types.constraint: cannot reasonably be violated: physics, hard legal limit, verified site condition
statement_types.requirement: an outcome the project is expected to satisfy
statement_types.preference: a desired outcome that may be traded against other goals
statement_types.assumption: a provisional belief used while evidence is incomplete

statement_model.rule: Test: who could relax this? A statement relaxable_by a stakeholder has basis stakeholder_choice and is not a constraint. Pressure toward a stronger type is recorded with pressured_by, never silently applied.

driver_rule: Depth follows feasibility intensity: at light depth, trigger and initiator suffice; standard and full add decision power, interests and pressures. Drivers are asked, never imputed: the AI may not attribute a motive to a party. A received brief is an output of its drivers; the inquiry may trace it backward before moving forward.

sources: premises of current design hypotheses that are not resolved positively
required questions of the current or an earlier phase that are unanswered
awareness_model.ranking: dependents x severity; severity 3 for negative or conflicting premises, 2 for unknown or insufficient, 1 for unanswered questions
awareness_model.budget: at most one awareness question per design turn
awareness_model.timing: surfaced at a natural pause (end of a design move), never mid-thought
awareness_model.queue: awareness items are queued and re-ranked; never dropped
awareness_model.blocking: awareness never blocks exploration; it blocks only through phase_model.commitment_rule
